**Setup.** Let g(x) = x²f(x) − 1. It has degree 9 and vanishes at r_n = n(n+1) for n = 1, …, 8. Write g(x) = c·P(x)(x − a), where P(x) = ∏(x − r_n).

**Conditions at 0.** Since x²f(x) has no constant or linear term, g(0) = −1 and g′(0) = 0.

- g′(0) = 0 gives a = P(0)/P′(0). Because P′(0)/P(0) = −Σ1/r_n = −(1 − 1/9) = −8/9, we get a = −9/8.
- g(0) = −1 gives c·P(0)·(9/8) = −1, so c = −8/(9P(0)).

Both match the proposed solution.

**Evaluate at 90.** Here 90 − a = 729/8, so g(90) = −81·P(90)/P(0). Then

f(90) − 1/90² = g(90)/90² = −P(90)/(100·P(0)).

**The ratio.** 90 − n(n+1) = (9 − n)(n + 10), so

P(90) = ∏(9 − n)(n + 10) = 8! · (18!/10!).

P(0) = ∏ n(n+1) = 8! · 9!.

The ratio is 18!/(10!·9!) = C(18,9)/10 = 48620/10 = 4862.

**Result.** f(90) − 1/90² = −4862/100 = −2431/50, which matches the proposed answer.
